title.narrative: Assuring the Future of Forests with Integrated Risk Management (AFFIRM) Mechanism

description.narrative:
1. Background and Rationale
Rising global priority of forest-related disasters: As climate change intensifies, forest-related disasterssuch as wildfires, landslides, and floodsare increasing in both frequency and severity. Disaster risk management has thus become a key global priority, and nature-based solutions (NbS) utilizing forests are increasingly recognized as effective approaches for integrated prevention and response. Growing demand from developing countries: Partner countries, including Cambodia, Thailand, and Viet Nam, have strong commitment to improving forest disaster management. However, limited policy capacity, technical expertise, and data availability constrain implementation. There is an urgent need for internationally aligned management roadmaps to protect carbon sinks and ensure community safety. Need for global cooperation and standardization: As forest disasters often transcend borders, coordinated international responses are essential. Establishing integrated mechanisms that link national statistics, policies, and operational systemswhile enabling regional information-sharingis critical. Cooperation with organizations such as the Food and Agriculture Organization is therefore essential.
2. Policy Alignment
Alignment with national ODA strategies: The project aligns with Koreas Fourth Basic Plan for International Development Cooperation (non-grant sector) and the Third Basic Plans strategy to lead green transition. It contributes to the Green ODA agenda by strengthening climate adaptation and mitigation capacity through integrated forest management. Contribution to global agendas: The project supports Koreas leadership in global climate action and contributes to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by enhancing adaptive capacity in developing countries.
3. Project Objectives
Enhancing climate resilience and livelihoods: The project aims to establish integrated forest risk management (IFM) systems to reduce disaster impacts and protect lives, livelihoods, and ecosystems. Strengthening cooperation and knowledge-sharing: It seeks to develop forest disaster data systems and promote regional and global partnerships, reinforcing Koreas role in climate resilience initiatives.
4. Implementation Approach and Project Components
Policy and analytical system development: The project will assess forest disaster governance and support evidence-based forest fire management strategies based on Review and Analysis reports. Capacity building through IFM training: Digital learning tools, including e-learning on early warning and risk assessment, will be developed using FAOs technical networks. Field-based pilot implementation: Vulnerable areas in four partner countries will be selected as pilot sites to establish community-based management models, alongside the provision of essential wildfire prevention and suppression equipment. Linkage with the Global Fire Management Hub: In cooperation with FAO Forestry, the Global Fire Management Hub will be utilized to share knowledge and disseminate outcomes.
5. Key Outputs
Policy and strategy documents: Governance assessment reports and national strategies, such as Cambodias National Forest Fire Strategic Plan and Lao PDRs National Forest Fire Roadmap. IFM knowledge products: Development of governance guidelines, e-learning courses, and analytical inputs for Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Community-based fire management models: Training-of-trainers programs and provision of wildfire prevention and suppression equipment, including protective gear and communication tools.
6. Expected Outcomes
Forest conservation and carbon sequestration: Integrated management systems will reduce forest degradation and maintain carbon sinks. Enhanced community resilience: Community-led disaster management systems will protect livelihoods and strengthen local adaptive capacity. Strengthened international standing
